verdict.rationale: Hightouch documents its own automation: syncs run "on the schedule or trigger you set" and can fire "when data changes," and marketers can build automated journeys. AI Decisioning agents also bundle scheduling rules and guardrails. The evidence never details how users define event-based rules (conditions on tracked events that fire specific actions), so only part of the story is shown. Missing for 10: documented event-condition rule definition (e.g., journey entry on a tracked event), trigger types and configuration depth, and hands-on or independent corroboration of event-triggered automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: A sync runs on the schedule or trigger you set, then reports the outcome of each run so you can confirm it worked.
Sync modeled data to sales, support, analytics, and internal tools on a schedule or when data changes.
Create audiences from warehouse data, build automated journeys
Each agent combines everything a campaign needs to learn and improve: an audience, goals, messages, scheduling rules, and guardrails.
